=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Package (Harbourglass / Paperbark Analytics)

**Scope note:** The Seller's cover material says [STANDARD] clauses have been "cleared" and need no scrutiny. That is the Seller's characterisation, not an agreed position, so I have reviewed every clause. Several "standard" items are where the largest buyer exposures sit.

## 1. Headline view

The package is not balanced. It combines a low general cap, a deductible basket, a short claims period, a sweeping data-room disclosure, and an anti-sandbagging clause. Together these would leave the Buyer with almost no effective warranty recourse for the risks the data room already shows. Most identified exposures are also disclosed, which removes them from warranty claims altogether, so they need specific indemnities or price adjustments.

## 2. Known exposures versus the Seller's protection

| Item | Identified exposure | Seller's proposed treatment | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility (DD-003) | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, security in place | Release "following Completion" | Repay at Completion from price (debt-free); payoff letter and discharge at Completion |
| Bluefen consent (DD-002) | ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) at risk | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Condition precedent with walk right |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k, plus payroll tax and super on-costs (not quantified) | Not in funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Seller-borne transaction cost, deducted from price |
| Ironquay SOW3 (DD-004, DD-010) | AUD 180k open; IP transfer conditional on payment | Limited indemnity for SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Pay pre-Completion; confirmatory IP assignment; specific IP indemnity |
| Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011) | AUD 330k aggregate | "Ordinary course" | Verify; treat as Seller cost or require Buyer consent |
| Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | ~1,240 records (personal information); scope and notifiability unknown | "Not expected to be material" | Specific indemnity, forensic completion, notifiable data breach assessment before Completion |
| Office lease (DD-007) | Unknown consent requirement | Notification obligation only | Confirm; landlord consent as Completion deliverable if needed |
| Mossvale (DD-009) | Unknown consent requirement | Silent | Confirm; consent as Completion deliverable if needed |

**Cap arithmetic:** Riverlark (3.2m) plus the bonuses (0.42m) plus the Sandbar renewals (0.33m) plus the Ironquay balance (0.18m) comes to about AUD 4.13m before on-costs. These are largely disclosed, so they would not be recoverable as warranty claims in any event. The AUD 4.8m general cap is therefore not a meaningful protection for the Buyer.

## 3. Clause-by-clause issues

### Cap (cl. 12.1): 20% of price, AUD 4.8m
- Too low for a AUD 24m deal with this disclosure profile. Push for at least 30%, ideally 100% of price for title, capacity, tax, and fraud.
- Known items should sit outside the warranty cap entirely and be dealt with by specific indemnities.

### Thresholds (cl. 12.2): AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket
- The basket is a deductible: only the excess above AUD 250k is recoverable. Push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recovery from the first dollar), a lower de minimis (AUD 10k or less), and aggregation of related claims.
- Clarify whether below-de minimis claims count towards the basket. The Seller's wording is ambiguous.
- Warranty and tax thresholds should not apply to title, capacity, tax, or specific indemnities.
- Effective maximum recovery under the Seller's terms is roughly AUD 4.55m (cap less basket), not AUD 4.8m.

### Time limits (cl. 12.3 / 13): 18 months; all limitations apply to all claims
- 18 months is short. Market practice for general warranties is typically 24 to 36 months, which would give time to observe the Bluefen, Riverlark, and privacy outcomes.
- Tax claims should run to the statute of limitations plus a buffer (usually 60 days after assessment).
- Reject the proposal that all limitations apply to all claims. Title and capacity should have a longer period (at least six years, or the statute of limitations).
- The privacy incident may generate regulatory activity beyond 18 months. Specific indemnity claims for it should have their own period.

### Fundamental / title warranties
- Rejecting the Seller's proposal that capacity and title be subject to general caps and time limits. Title and capacity are the most basic protections a share buyer has; they should be capped at full price, outside de minimis and basket, and survive for the longer period.

### Limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance (cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- Apply "to all Claims of any nature" is too broad. Carve out fraud, title, tax, specific indemnities, and wilful misconduct.
- Non-reliance and exclusive-remedy clauses should not exclude fraud. Confirm with NSW counsel how far any such exclusion would be effective given the Australian Consumer Law misleading-conduct provisions and general misrepresentation principles.

### Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2)
- **Reject general disclosure of the whole data room and public registers.** Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room, including DD-002 to DD-012. That would disclose virtually anything and render the warranties hollow. Disclosure should be specific, fairly disclosed, and against a specific warranty.
- The data room is stated as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Require a bring-down disclosure and updated data room index as a condition of signing.
- The Seller's clause 1.4 (no admission of breach or liability) is acceptable on its own terms.

### Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3): no claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in data room or public records
- This is an anti-sandbagging clause and is unacceptable. Combined with the general disclosure, it would bar claims for almost everything the Buyer has reviewed, which is most of the diligence.
- Counter-position: the Buyer's knowledge should not prejudice warranty claims. At most, specific written disclosure in the Disclosure Letter should qualify warranties. Specific indemnities must apply regardless of knowledge.

### Bluefen conditions (cl. 3 / 6.3)
- The Bluefen change-control consent (cl. 11.2) has conditions in cl. 11.3 that are not satisfied. The Seller's position is to treat consent as satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent", which may not require the conditions to be met.
- Push for:
  - A condition precedent to Completion: final written consent, unconditional or with only Buyer-acceptable conditions, and evidence the cl. 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - A Buyer right to terminate if not obtained by a long-stop date.
  - If the Buyer waives, a price holdback or escrow tied to revenue retention.
  - An obligation on the Seller (not reasonable endeavours) to procure the consent, with the cost borne by the Seller.

### Riverlark (cl. 2 / 7)
- A post-Completion release of a AUD 3.2m secured facility is unacceptable. In a debt-free/cash-free deal, the debt must be settled at Completion out of the price.
- Require: a payoff letter, a deed of release or discharge of security, PPSR discharge (or undertaking to deliver), and deduction of the payoff from the price in the funds flow.
- Confirm whether Riverlark's change-control clause (cl. 8.1) needs consent.

### Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1)
- The "adequate" characterisation is wrong. The IP transfer is conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee (DD-004 cl. 7.3). AUD 180k is open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- Push for: Seller payment of all open SOW3 amounts before Completion (or deduction from price as a debt-like item); a confirmatory IP assignment as a Completion deliverable; a specific IP indemnity for third-party claims and any defect in title, outside the general cap; and an IP warranty that the Company owns the Project Materials free of conditions.
- Note the disclosure is not independent bank verification of non-payment. Obtain Seller evidence.

### Employee bonuses (DD-005, funds flow)
- AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are not in the funds flow. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller", but they will be paid by the Company post-Completion if conditions are met, so the Buyer bears the cost.
- Push for: a Seller-borne transaction cost deducted from price in the funds flow; the Seller to bear employer on-costs (NSW payroll tax at the applicable rate; superannuation guarantee, currently 12%); a specific indemnity for any bonus or change-of-control entitlement; and confirmation of which employees are covered.
- Indicative exposure: AUD 420k plus roughly AUD 50k superannuation and up to ~AUD 25k payroll tax, subject to confirming rates and eligibility.

### Funds flow
- The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics". It does not reflect the Riverlark payoff, the bonuses, the SOW3 balance, or the Sandbar renewals. A debt-free/cash-free price needs these items to be expressly treated as debt or debt-like.
- Push for completion accounts with debt and working capital adjustments, or a locked-box with a leakage covenant. Whichever mechanism is used, Riverlark, bonuses, and SOW3 must appear.

### Privacy/export incident (DD-006, Disclosure 6)
- The Seller says the incident is preliminary and "not expected to be material". That is not a basis for accepting the risk. Around 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles, and activity timestamps are personal information under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
- Push for: a forensic investigation completed before Completion; a Seller warranty that no other incidents exist; a formal notifiable data breach assessment (the Company should confirm whether it is an APP entity and whether the eligible-data-breach test is met); a specific uncapped (or price-capped) indemnity covering notification costs, regulatory action, and third-party claims; an escrow or holdback; and Buyer control of regulatory engagement post-Completion.

### Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Neither the Seller nor the disclosure confirms whether consent is needed for the share sale. Require written landlord and Mossvale confirmation that no consent is needed or, if needed, make it a Completion deliverable.

### Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011)
- The three renewals, each AUD 110k, total AUD 330k. The disclosure reads them "together for timing/scope", which suggests they may be connected and possibly structured to fall below thresholds. Push back on "ordinary course" as a characterisation.
- Push for: a full list of contracts and terms; confirmation of whether they bind the Company post-Completion; an interim operating covenant requiring Buyer consent to renewals or new commitments above a set threshold; and treatment of any unavoidable renewal costs as a price adjustment.

### Tax and IP warranties
- The Seller considers the tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime". They are not settled. Tax needs a specific pre-Completion tax indemnity uncapped to price with the extended tax period. IP needs full warranties (ownership, non-infringement, no encumbrances) at a higher cap.

### Title (DD-012)
- The share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100%. That is the starting point, not verification.
- Obtain a current ASIC company extract, inspect the original register, confirm no PPSR or other security over the shares, check the constitution for transfer restrictions, and obtain board approval of the transfer.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1 (deal-breakers):**
1. Reject general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Require specific disclosure and a bring-down as at signing.
2. Reject the anti-sandbagging clause (cl. 8.3).
3. Make Bluefen consent a condition precedent, with a walk right and long-stop date.
4. Repay Riverlark at Completion from the price, with discharge of security. No post-Completion release.
5. Put Ironquay SOW3 payment and confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverables.

**Priority 2 (specific indemnities and price):**
6. Specific, uncapped (or price-capped) indemnities for: the privacy incident; the bonuses and on-costs; the Ironquay IP; the Sandbar renewals; the lease and Mossvale; and pre-Completion tax.
7. Treat bonuses, SOW3 balance, and Riverlark as debt or debt-like items; fix the funds flow.
8. Completion accounts or locked-box with leakage protection.

**Priority 3 (limits and timing):**
9. Raise the general cap to at least 30% of price; full price for title, capacity, tax, and fraud.
10. Replace the deductible basket with a tipping basket and reduce the de minimis (AUD 10k or lower).
11. Extend general claims to 24 to 36 months; tax to the statute of limitations plus 60 days; title and capacity to six years or more.
12. Carve title, capacity, tax, fraud, and specific indemnities out of all limitations, exclusive-remedy, and non-reliance clauses.
13. Reject the "all limitations apply to all claims" drafting.

**Priority 4 (verification):**
14. Full title verification (ASIC extract, PPSR search, register inspection, constitution review).
15. Confirm consent requirements for the lease and Mossvale.
16. Obtain evidence of SOW3 payment status and Sandbar contract terms.
17. Forensic report and notifiable data breach assessment for the privacy incident.

**Caveats:** This is a commercial and legal issues review to support the mark-up, not a final opinion. Confirm NSW-specific points (stamp duty, Australian Consumer Law effect on non-reliance, payroll tax rates, and Privacy Act obligations) with the deal's NSW counsel before the mark-up goes out.
